subtitle: a fingernail-sized source of terahertz waves

effect: in very clean materials electrons flow like a viscous liquid
how: Terahertz waves see through clothing, packaging and the top layers of skin, and could carry far faster wireless data, but making them takes bulky lasers or deep cold. In ultra-clean graphene the electrons flow like a thick liquid, and pushing them fast through a narrow channel makes that liquid ripple like a flag in the wind; the ripples throw off terahertz waves from a chip the size of a fingernail.
obstacle: The ripple instability has been predicted for decades but has never been shown to give useful power.
why: Graphene terahertz detectors exist; an electron-fluid emitter has never worked.
real: Multiple theory papers model Dyakonov-Shur THz emission from hydrodynamic graphene electrons and note it has never been observed experimentally.
